articles.headline: Who is Joe Fagnano? Meet Ravens undrafted QB replacing injured Lamar Jackson, Tyler Huntley
keyFacts: Ravens quarterbacks Lamar Jackson and Tyler Huntley both left Sunday's game against the Bills with injuries.
Undrafted rookie quarterback Joe Fagnano entered the game as Baltimore's emergency third-string quarterback.
Fagnano may see future playing time if Jackson and Huntley remain sidelined.
body: On Sunday, the Ravens dealt with an NFL nightmare scenario the day after Halloween: a quarterback room down multiple names.

Not only did Lamar Jackson exit after his first throw of the day against the Bills, but later on, top backup Tyler Huntley also left the game with an injury. Both were ruled out, leaving Baltimore to turn to its emergency third quarterback.
That would be undrafted rookie Joe Fagnano, who took the reins of the Ravens' offense in a huge matchup against the Bills.
Here's some background of Fagnano, who may even be forced into future playing time if Jackson and Huntley remain sidelined.
MORE: How long will Lamar Jackson be out with thumb injury?
Who is Joe Fagnano?

Fagnano is a 25-year-old undrafted rookie quarterback for the Ravens. The Williamsport, Pennsylvania, native stands at 6-3 and 230 pounds, signing with the Ravens in the aftermath of the 2026 NFL Draft.
Since then, Fagnano has been buried on the depth chart behind Jackson and Huntley, but Sunday presented an opportunity for him to prove himself.

In college, Fagnano emerged as a potential NFL prospect during his 2025 season at UConn, throwing for 28 touchdowns and just one interception. Now, he's suddenly in the NFL spotlight, taking starting snaps for the Ravens.

Joe Fagnano college

Fagnano arrived at the University of Maine as a walk-on, but quickly earned a scholarship and became the team's starter in his first collegiate season in 2019. He would remain at Maine — an FCS program — for four seasons, though he was held to just eight games combined between 2020 and 2021.

After the 2022 season, Fagnano transferred to UConn to become an FBS quarterback, where he would start for the next few years. A shoulder injury ended his 2023 season early, but he fully emerged in 2025 for his best season yet with the Huskies.

articles.headline: Bernie Sanders gives blazing interview as support for California billionaire tax plummets: ‘Disgusting’
keyFacts: A poll showed that 52.6% of voters oppose California's Proposition 40, a proposed one-time 5% billionaire wealth tax.
Senator Bernie Sanders criticized wealthy donors opposing the measure, claiming they prioritize protecting fortunes over funding children's healthcare.
Google co-founder Sergey Brin has spent more than $100 million opposing Proposition 40, filings show.
body: Sen. Bernie Sanders has lashed out at deep-pocketed donors protecting their fortunes for a drop in support for the California billionaire tax.

Sanders, responding to a poll showing more voters are against the measure than in favor, claimed that West Coast billionaires had become $500 billion richer in the last year and criticized what he described as efforts to protect their fortunes while children lack healthcare.

“They are doing phenomenally well and really [it] is quite disgusting, to my mind, that they think it’s more important that they hang on to their $200 billion rather than make sure the kids of California have health care,” he told KCRA’s Ashley Zavala in an interview Sunday.

Thanks for signing up!

Proposition 40, described as a one-time 5% wealth tax on billionaires that would primarily fund healthcare, was opposed by 52.6% of voters, while 34.5% supported it and 11.5% were undecided, according to a California Post poll conducted by McLaughlin & Associates.
Sanders framed the results as part of a broader fight over wealth and access to care. “The fact of the matter is, we have more income and wealth inequality in America today,” he said.
Pollster John McLaughlin offered a different explanation for the measure’s weakness, saying voters distrust state lawmakers on taxes.

“Voters just don’t trust Sacramento politicians when it comes to taxes. Whenever pollsters ask should we raise taxes on billionaires? People say why not but naturally when we ask should they raise taxes on you? People say no — especially when affordability is the top issue,” said pollster John McLaughlin.

Google co-founder Sergey Brin, the world’s fourth-richest person, is among those who are spending money to block Proposition 40. He has spent more than $100 million opposing California’s proposed billionaire tax, which could cost him an estimated $13.3 billion.

Brin, whose fortune is estimated at about $267 billion, recently donated an additional $20 million to Build a Better California, an organization campaigning against the tax, according to a recent filing.

articles.headline: Mexican Formula One Grand Prix: Kimi Antonelli aims to seal title – live
keyFacts: Lewis Hamilton secured his first pole position for Ferrari and his 105th career pole during qualifying for the Mexico City Grand Prix.
George Russell joined Hamilton on the front row after taking second place in qualifying, with Kimi Antonelli starting in fourth.
Kimi Antonelli remains positioned to claim his first world championship during the race, though Russell and Hamilton must win to keep their title hopes alive.
body: Lap 18 of 71: Leclerc now has 4.4 seconds over Verstappen, who’s on medium tires. Then Hamilton is another 2.0 back – while his complaints aren’t unwarranted, he hasn’t made any progress chasing down Verstappen while on softer tires.

Lap 15 of 71: Hamilton is informed of the five-second Leclerc penalty. He immediately notes that Leclerc is still getting the benefit of clean air. Indeed he does, and he’s making the most of it – the gap to Verstappen and Hamilton is growing.
Lap 14 of 71: And now George Russell gets a 10-second penalty. He’ll likely lose out to the McLarens of Norris and Piastri. Norris has him in his sights already.

Lap 12 of 71: Piastri zips past Lindblad like a Maryland driver on the Capital Beltway. (If you know, you know.) He’s up to seventh, a nice recovery from yesterday, and if some of the people ahead of him are penalized, he’ll move up more.
Lap 11 of 71: George Russell is under investigation for the opening contact with Hadjar. Three of the top five drivers have the telltale exclamation point by their names on the F1 graphic.
Lap 10 of 71: Penalty or not – how does Ferrari let that happen? If Leclerc ends up penalized, they’ve handed control of the race to Verstappen, and he’s unlikely to give it back.
Lap 8 of 71: Will anyone pit this early in the race, knowing they won’t lose much time because of the Virtual Safety Car? Maybe if we were a few more laps into this race.
Lap 4 of 71: Hamilton inquires as to what action is being taken. He’s assured that people are looking into it.

8 Norris … oh, wait, he just passed Colapinto

Of note: Hadjar went all the way back to 22nd. That’s not good.
Colapinto roared up to seventh.
Oh – and the guy who’s about to be the youngest F1 champion ever is still in fourth. Verstappen went ahead of him, but Russell had a lackluster start and is now fifth.

Hamilton leads … but here comes teammate Leclerc, madly challenging! Leclerc goes way off the track but is now in the lead pending whatever Ferrari and F1 say. Verstappen took advantage of the intra-Ferrari battle to sail into second.
On the radio: Hamilton says he got pushed out by his own teammate. He’s not wrong.
Tires or tyres: Most drivers are opening on softs, but Nico Hülkenberg and a few others further down the grid are on mediums. Intriguingly, so is Max Verstappen, who starts fifth.
Calling on readers to answer these thought experiments:

1. Are we looking at the beginning of a Kimi Antonelli era, or will we see Max Verstappen or Lando Norris fighting back next year? Or maybe one of the Ferrari drivers – Charles Leclerc and Lewis Hamilton, who has taken a few steps back toward championship form this year?

2. Where does a 20-year-old F1 champion fit in terms of precocious athlete accomplishments? Do we compare it with Pele winning his first World Cup at age 17? Should we only consider individuals, like a 20-year-old Mike Tyson winning the heavyweight championship? Maybe Mikaela Shiffrin’s breakthrough at age 17? Garry Kasparov holding the world chess championship and becoming the world’s top-ranked player at age 22? Justin Bieber having hits at age 15?

3. How did Haas replace Esteban Ocon’s livery so quickly? (To answer a question from earlier: Yes, the F1 graphics team got Ryo Harikawa into the pre-race montage. “Congratulations on your debut, now before you attempt qualifying for the first time in your life, can you stand in front of this green screen and look cool?”)

One distinguishing characteristic of the Autódromo Hermanos Rodríguez is the distance from the starting line to Turn 1. Then it’s right, left, right into another long straightaway, then some sharp turns before a shorter straightaway. Then they’ll veer left into a set of long, arcing curves, a short straight, a sharp right and then a near-hairpin turn before a complicated series of curves to take the drivers back to the starting line.

Another unique aspect – altitude. Denver is the Mile High City, but Mexico City is the Two Kilometer High City, which is considerably less catchy. Race engineers describe have to factor thin air into account.
The weather will be in the mid-20s Celsius, which in Fahrenheit is “pretty nice.” The track temperature will be approximately Venusian.

Lindblad, Gasly and Hulkenberg all moved up due to Liam Lawson’s disqualification from qualifying, which will place the Racing Bulls driver at the back of the grid, even behind Valtteri Bottas, whose engine overhaul incurred a 50-place penalty for an engine overhaul but in reality isn’t being punished at all because he was 21st in qualifying, anyway.

The other item of note on the grid: Ryo Hirakawa will make his F1 race debut on short notice, replacing Esteban Ocon after the lame-duck driver (to be replaced by Rafael Câmara next year) had a flareup with Haas management at a practice session. Hirakawa will start 18th after besting Lance Stroll, home-country hero Sergio Perez and Perez’s Cadillac teammate Bottas in qualifying.

That leads us to one moment of suspense: Can F1’s media team update its driver intro to include Hiwakawa? The video is best known for featuring Bottas’ mustache, Stroll smiling smugly as if daring his critics to keep talking, and a vivid look at the age difference between the graybeards (Bottas, eternal journeyman Nico Hülkenberg, seven-time champion Lewis Hamilton and two-time champion Fernando Alonso) and fresh-faced youngsters such as Antonelli, Lindblad, Gabriel Bortoleto and Oliver Bearman.
I preferred last year’s video, if only because Alonso seemed to be doing a capable impression of The World’s Most Interesting Man.

There are still several ways Kimi Antonelli could be denied the F1 championship this year.
- George Russell could win all five remaining races while Antonelli picks up a total of just one point (10th place in any race).
- Lewis Hamilton could win all five remaining races while Antonelli picks up no points.
- Antonelli could decide to retire at age 20 and petition to retroactively forfeit his results from this year.
- AI agents could decide to shut down all the race computers for every F1 team in a bid to curb fuel consumption and Kim Kardashian’s screen time.
- Aliens could beam Antonelli back to his home planet.
- The entire year could be written off as Pamela Ewing’s dream, like the ninth season of the nighttime TV soap Dallas.
- Time travelers from the year 2053 may arrive in February 2026 and defeat Antonelli in several races in the new timeline.

Barring any of those scenarios, Antonelli will displace Sebastian Vettel as the youngest F1 champion in history. Barring an Antonelli catastrophe and a win by either Russell or Hamilton, that championship will be decided today.
Meanwhile, Hamilton is on the pole for the first time in three years.
Beau will be here shortly. In the meantime, here’s Giles Richards on how qualifying went down on Saturday:

Even as Formula One’s young gun Kimi Antonelli remains on course to claim his first world championship on Sunday it was the veteran, seven-time champion Lewis Hamilton who gave a salutary reminder that there is very much fight left in the old dog yet as he claimed a spectacular pole position for the Mexico City Grand Prix.

Hamilton delivered a superb lap for Ferrari to secure his first pole for the team and just beat Mercedes’ George Russell into second. World champion in waiting Antonelli was in fourth place but remains in position to close out the title on Sunday, although Hamilton and Russell, who must win the race to have any hope of keeping the fight alive, have at least locked out the front row.

It was clearly a hugely emotional moment for Hamilton at the Autódromo Hermanos Rodríguez to finally nail the top spot for Ferrari in his second season with the team, with the 41-year-old’s 105th pole also his first since 2023.
“Thank you so much, that’s been such a long time coming,” he said. “That feels good. I’m lost for words. My first pole with Ferrari. 105 poles, I like that number.

“Where there’s a will, there’s a way. It’s all in the mind. For sure, you might feel aches and pains, luckily I don’t, I do all those different things to keep myself young and fit. But I love what I do, and love is not gone.”

articles.headline: Alaska Sen. Sullivan warns alleged ‘Decoy Dan’ scheme is working: ‘I’m going to lose a lot of votes to that trickery’
keyFacts: Alaska Sen. Dan Sullivan claimed allies of candidate Peltola recruited a decoy candidate to trick voters.
Peltola's former campaign manager claimed Peltola knew about the scheme, which the Justice Department is now investigating.
Sen. Sullivan stated he will accept Tuesday's election results, but Representative Comer warned Peltola might not be seated if she wins.
body: “Their first order of business, like I said, is, ‘How can we trick people in Alaska so they can throw the vote in a way that’s certainly deceitful, if not illegal, towards Peltola?'” the Republican senator vented to CNN’s “State of the Union.”
“By the way, their scheme is working,” he said. “They got the decoy guy on the ballot. I’m sure I’m going to lose a lot of votes to that trickery.”

Peltola, a former congresswoman, has been slammed by bombshell revelations from the New York Times that her allies worked to recruit retired public-school teacher Dan J. Sullivan, now known as “Decoy Dan,” to run for the Senate seat, too.
Although she has denied involvement, the outlet quoted her former campaign manager, Elisa Rios, who claimed Peltola was “definitely aware.”
Rios had been pushed out of the campaign during an August reshuffling, along with other top staff.
“Decoy Dan” is registered as a Republican, despite voting Democrat in recent presidential election cycles and reportedly having a magnet of far-left revolutionary Che Guevara on his refrigerator.

For months, both “Decoy Dan” and Peltola’s camp had denied a connection between her team and his decision to run, but the outlet also found other staffers on her old campaign operation and the Democratic Congressional Campaign Committee and text messages to identify a connection.
A Dem operative named Jerid Kurtz had reportedly searched for another Dan Sullivan to recruit for the election.
“This is treating the people of my state with utter disrespect and disdain,” Sen. Sullivan told CNN. “And I don’t think it’s worthy of a US senator or a US Senate candidate.”

The Justice Department has been ramping up its probe into whether any laws were broken with the presence of “Decoy Dan” on the Alaska ballot. The DOJ also sued to stop certification of the election if Sen. Sullivan loses.
House Oversight Committee Chairman James Comer (R-Ky.) said Sunday that it’s possible Peltola won’t be seated if she wins the Senate race because of the controversy.
But despite that and other GOP honchos equivocating on whether they will accept the results on Tuesday, Sen. Sullivan made it clear that he will not fight the outcome, however unfair it might be.
“I’m going to accept the election results,” he replied.
“Don’t let this election be stolen,” he later added, addressing Alaskan voters before Tuesday’s vote.
Peltola currently has a 2 percentage-point edge over Sen. Sullivan in the latest RealClearPolitics aggregate of polls.
Alaska has a unique election system where the top four candidates appear on the general election ballot and are decided through ranked-choice voting.
Peltola’s campaign did not respond to a Post request for comment.

articles.headline: How to get the Pirate Shop Access Token in Fortnite Chapter 7 mini season
keyFacts: The Pirate Shop Access Token is a rare item in the Fortnite Chapter 7 mini season that grants 14 days of free item shop purchases.
Players can find the token by opening transformed treasure chests, which have a small chance of dropping the special loot.
Activating the token provides two tokens for 2026 and 2027, letting players claim most cosmetics for free permanently.
body: The Pirate Shop Access Token is a new item introduced in the Fortnite Chapter 7 mini season, and it allows you to get anything from the Shop for free for a 14-day period.

Anything sold for V-Bucks in the Fortnite item shop can be claimed for free, meaning any outfit, pickaxe, back bling, sidekick, kicks, and more are yours to have forever. The item is too good to be true, so of course, it's extremely difficult to get your hands on.
Here's how to get the Pirate Shop Token in Fortnite Chapter 7 mini season.
How to get the Pirate Shop Token in Fortnite Chapter 7 mini season

The process of getting the Pirate Shop Token is just like every other item in Fortnite, you need to open a treasure chest. Regular chests have been transformed into treasure chests in the mini season, so you don't need to be on the hunt for anything special. However, when you open a treasure chest, you have a small chance of finding special loot for yourself and everyone in your party. In most cases, your special loot will be a gizmo, like the Sprite Locator or the Portable Extractor. For the lucky few, your special loot will be a Pirate Shop Access Token.

In the tweet above from user Snowslept, you'll see that the chest will have a unique animation featuring a gold explosion, and a banner will appear on your screen saying that you found pirate shop access. You'll gain two Pirate Shop Access Tokens, one for 2026 and the other for 2027. When you activate the token, you'll have 14 days to claim anything from the Fortnite item shop for free. Essentially, any cosmetic is yours for the taking, but you can only claim sidekicks once. The only things you cannot purchase are real money offers (like V-Bucks and bundles), gifts, and pass levels/rewards.
If you're hunting for the Pirate Shop Access token, your best bet is to land in any of the following locations:
- Arlong Park
- Lantern Landing
- Rubber Resort
- Fortune's Fort
- Loguetown
- Plunder Port
- Busy Bay

We personally recommend landing at Arlong Park or Lantern Landing as they're fairly close to one another, and you can quickly make your way down to Windmill Village and Loguetown. If you're quick, you can open upwards of 50 chests a game.

articles.headline: Democrat endorses Republican candidate in key Michigan Senate race as party spat escalates
keyFacts: Democrat Haley Stevens endorsed Republican candidate Mike Rogers in Michigan's Senate race following a feud with Democratic nominee Abdul El-Sayed.
The Michigan Senate race is a key battleground contest that analysts say will help decide control of Congress.
Tuesday's midterm elections will decide which political party controls Congress for the next two years.
body: - Published
A Democrat in Michigan has endorsed the Republican candidate in the state's crucial US Senate contest, as a spat with her own party's candidate Abdul El-Sayed escalated just days before the vote.
Haley Stevens, a sitting congresswoman who lost out on the Democratic Senate nomination to El-Sayed, made a surprise appearance alongside the Republican candidate Mike Rogers at a church on Sunday.

"I don't belong in Abdul's campaign," she said in a video posted to X shortly after that appearance. "Who we are as Michiganders is not hate and is not what we are getting out from our Democratic nominee right now."
"That's why I am endorsing Mike Rogers," Stevens said.
Stevens also said El-Sayed had apparently told her she was no longer welcome in his campaign.

"This is a very close election, we all know that, but Abdul made clear that I was not welcome in his campaign, that he didn't need me there, that he didn't want me there," Stevens told reporters after the Sunday church service.
The pair had been scheduled to appear together at a different event on Sunday, but El-Sayed reportedly asked her not to come.

They had clashed publicly over a campaign advert from an outside liberal group which blamed Israel for high food prices. El-Sayed criticised the advert and said he had nothing to do with its contents.
When asked about Stevens' endorsement, El-Sayed told reporters he was focused on the problems Michiganders are facing.
"At the end of the day, I don't think about Haley Stevens," he said. "None of this matters."

In downtown Detroit, people were grabbing lunch or making their way to Ford Field stadium for the Detroit Lions American football game when the news broke. Every democrat that the BBC spoke with shared that they were disappointed by her endorsement of Rogers.
Summer Lawrence, a 21-year-old student, told the BBC that Stevens' endorsement felt like a betrayal to the Democratic party and everything she told voters she stood for.
"I just genuinely don't understand it," she said. "I do think it's a betrayal of the party because the things she stands for are not the same things that he stands for as a Republican."
Matthew Barera, another Michigan voter told the BBC, he, too, did not understand Stevens' reasoning.
"I don't know if she had her own revenge or not, maybe she had frustrations with the party in her own elections," he said.
Others, including Republicans who support Rogers, said they doubted it would make a difference to the race.
"People can see right through her actions, you know? She's just angry," Marissa Lee, a Rogers supporter, told the BBC. "She is not going to make anybody change their mind."
The Michigan Senate race is considered by analysts to be one of the tightest in Tuesday's midterm elections, which will decide which party controls Congress for the next two years.
It is one of a handful of battleground contests that will ultimately decide control of the Senate.

The seat is currently held by a retiring Democrat and the last time a Republican was elected to this Senate seat was in 1994. But in presidential elections, it is one of the crucial swing states - Michigan voted for Democrat Joe Biden in 2020 but Trump in 2024.
Rogers welcomed Stevens' endorsement and said it showed "courage" during brief remarks with reporters outside the church.
President Donald Trump echoed that sentiment saying on Truth Social that, "[Stevens] showed great and almost unprecedented loyalty to the Great People of Michigan with what she did".

Many of Stevens' staff reportedly resigned immediately after her announcement, while the chair of the Democratic Party in Michigan said her decision "shows that she has abandoned everything she claims to care about".
"We reject the attempts by Stevens and bad-faith actors to divide our party and undermine our momentum," Curtis Hertel said in a statement.
Over the weekend, as Stevens' criticism of El-Sayed escalated, a number of Democratic politicians in Michigan publicly encouraged her to end the feud and back the party's candidates more directly.
"It feels like it's more about her feelings than Michiganders," State Senator Mallory McMorrow said on MSNow. "It is a choice between MAGA and Michigan. And I'm on team Michigan."
On Sunday, Democratic Senator Chuck Schumer called Stevens' endorsement of Rogers "a despicable betrayal" of her political party.

"Senate Democrats are united in our support for Abdul El-Sayed, because we know he will fight for the economic interests of working families in Michigan, unlike Mike Rogers, who is a tool of Donald Trump and billionaire donors," Schumer said.

After a bruising and sometimes bitter campaign earlier this year, El-Sayed, a left-wing outsider, defeated Stevens, the establishment-backed congresswoman, to win the party's nomination for the US Senate race.
The primary, and the pair's subsequent feud, has underlined divisions over the party's direction ahead of the 2028 presidential election.

articles.headline: Judge dismisses Trump attempt to block Alaska Senate race results if Republican loses

body: A judge has dismissed the Donald Trump-backed lawsuit seeking to block certification of Alaska’s US Senate race if Republican incumbent Dan Sullivan loses.

Trump said on 23 October that he had ordered the justice department to file the lawsuit in a move that voting rights experts called an “unprecedented intervention” by the federal government with control of Congress in the balance.

The justice department argued in its lawsuit, filed less than two weeks before election day, that there could be “voter confusion” over the presence of two candidates named Dan Sullivan on the November ballot, which Republicans fear could take away votes from the incumbent and influence the race’s outcome in favor of the Democratic nominee, Mary Peltola.
Sullivan, in an interview with CNN on Sunday morning, said that he would accept the results of his upcoming election.

According to a recent New York Times investigation, aides from Peltola’s campaign recruited another man who shared Sullivan’s name to join the race in a ploy to peel away votes from the Republican incumbent.

Since those revelations, Republicans, including Donald Trump, have called for Peltola to be disqualified from the race and criminally prosecuted. Peltola has continued to deny any knowledge of such a scheme on the part of her campaign, recently telling a reporter at a campaign event that she had “no idea” if any of her staff were involved.
Asked by CNN’s Jake Tapper if he would only accept the election results if he won, Sullivan responded: “No, I’m going to accept the election results.”

Earlier in his interview with Tapper, Sullivan also said he wasn’t focused on how Peltola’s campaign might be legally challenged. He was focused instead on winning the race outright. He nonetheless expressed doubt that Peltola had lacked any knowledge of the effort to put a second Dan Sullivan on the ballot.
“She’s continually lying to the Alaskan people,” Sullivan said. “And I guarantee you, she’s lying right now.”

Meanwhile, the Washington Post reported that Republicans tried to boost unviable Democratic candidates in the Alaska primaries as well. A Republican Super Pac boosted two candidates for Senate who did not live in Alaska, and praised them as “progressives” similar to Bernie Sanders.

body: Lisandro Martinez has been labelled ‘pathetic’ for his quickfire red card during Manchester United’s defeat at Chelsea.
Football writer Henry Winter also described the sending off as ‘almost mutinous’, as the centre-back picked up two yellow cards in the space of 83 seconds.

Martinez lost his man and ended up chasing after him to the back post and elbowing him in the face while not looking at the ball.
VAR recommended an on-field review for the foul and a penalty was awarded with a second yellow card for Martinez then coming.

And speaking with Shaun Custis on The Sunday Edition, he said: “This was just pathetic. 83 seconds, he gets rolled and turned by Morgan Rogers and manages to bring him down at the third time of asking.

“Then, he loses Fofana at the corner and leads with his elbow into him and is sent off. He quite rightly gets blanked by Michael Carrick as he goes down the tunnel, it is almost mutinous a red card like that.
“It is a case of what are you doing? I thought it was absolutely shocking.”
And Man United broadcaster Scott Saunders believes that the Argentine shouldn’t play for the club again.
Speaking on the talkSPORT Goals Show, he said: “This guy is an idiot. I know he likes to play on the edge, but that is pointless. It is pointless.
“The game is already gone because they are 1-0 down, but that is the icing on the cake.
Man United have won just one Premier League game all season AFP
“There isn’t loads of contact, but you are giving the referee a decision to make. I cannot get over this guy. This guy can’t play for Man United again.

“He is meant to be a leader in this team and if that is how leaders act, I dread to think where we are going. I cannot believe he has been that stupid.
“He shouldn’t be picked again.”
How did Carrick react to the red card?
Man United started the game the better of the two teams and should have scored at least a couple.
Bruno Fernandes and Amad Diallo were the biggest culprits with two sitters.
Man United are in a relegation battle at the moment Getty
Matheus Cunha also had a goal ruled out for offside, meaning the teams headed in at 0-0 only for Rogers to run through the middle of the defence and open the scoring with a deft chip.
Martinez was then sent off and Cole Palmer dispatched the penalty.

articles.headline: How to know if a USB-C cable is waterproof
keyFacts: Waterproof USB-C cables are identified by IEC Ingress Protection ratings, specifically IP67 or IP68 for dust and water resistance.
Water inside USB-C connectors can cause short circuits, equipment damage, or fires, so wet cables should never be plugged in.
Unplugged wet cables should be shaken and left to air dry for 24 to 48 hours before reuse if no corrosion appears.
body: How to know if a USB-C cable is waterproof
Always check the IP rating when purchasing a waterproof USB-C cable

Some USB-C cables are waterproof, but you need to learn to recognize which ones. Widely available from online retailers, including Amazon, they're likely to feature seals to protect the connection and ship in a variety of types, including male, female, and angled cables. But do the seals work? The International Electrotechnical Commission (IEC) has developed the IEC 60529 standard, a globally accepted Ingress Protection code that shows how well an enclosure (such as a USB-C plug) resists solids and liquids.

The first number in this code represents dust protection, while the second shows water protection. Under this code, waterproof USB-C cables should have an IP67 or IP68 rating. These cables are most frequently used in specific tough environments, such as manufacturing, construction, maritime and electric vehicle charging systems — anywhere exposed to water, weather or accident. When choosing a cable, what matters most is the IP rating (even for other gadgets, like your phone):
- IP67: A dust-tight cable that can handle being under up to one meter of water for up to 30 minutes.
- IP68: A dust-tight cable suitable for continuous immersion, typically beyond 1 meter, though this varies by manufacturer.
What are the risks of USB water exposure?

The USB-C standard does not specify water resistance, which means that while ordinary cables may survive a splash, nothing is guaranteed and water exposure comes with some risks. USB-C is versatile, ubiquitous and complex. Take a connector apart, and you'll find it contains 24 contacts, which may connect to data or power wires inside the cable. (That's 20 more pins than found in USB-A, which helps account for the faster data transfers.) If water gets inside the connector, it can cause a short circuit that may damage your equipment, while long-term moisture exposure can corrode contacts. There's also the risk that short-circuited wet cables can overheat, potentially causing a fire. You should never plug a wet cable — even a waterproof one — into a device.

USB cable protection is usually achieved with a silicone rubber seal, gasket, or locking collar around the connector to protect against water ingress. Some rely on threaded bayonet couplings, with a rubber seal that compresses as the collar is tightened, creating a watertight link. Cables designed for extended water exposure may use a tough synthetic rubber, such as neoprene. An even tougher material called fluoroelastomer (FKM) is frequently used where chemical or solvent resistance is required.
Can you use a wet cable once it dries?

If the contacts show no corrosion, you can generally use the cable safely again once it dries. To dry a cable, unplug it, shake the connector ends to force water out, and let it dry for 24 to 48 hours. Don't try to dry the cable with a hair dryer, as the heat can damage the cable, and don't use rice, as it can introduce grit and dust into the connector. If a cable becomes hot when using it after drying, replace it.

Brands of waterproof cables, such as Atlavox, Yale, and the more industrial-grade L-Com, are available at good DIY/tech retailers and also at Amazon. You should ensure the cable you choose is IP-rated, rather than simply being water resistant. Basic waterproof cables are available for around ten dollars, while ultra-rugged waterproof cables for the toughest environments can cost ten times that. Finally, when purchasing one of these cables, you should always check the official IP rating, as a cable that doesn't provide this may not deliver what you need.

body: Rep. Haley Stevens’s (D-MI) chief of staff has resigned after the Democratic congresswoman endorsed Republican candidate Mike Rogers for Senate in Michigan .

Justin German, who has served as Stevens’s chief of staff since she first took office in the House in January 2019, said “many members” of Stevens’ staff, including himself, resigned on Sunday. He cited Stevens’s endorsement of Rogers, which came just two days ahead of Election Day, as her feud with Democratic Senate candidate Abdul el Sayed quickly escalated throughout the weekend.

“As Haley Stevens’ Chief of Staff for eight years, I speak on behalf of our team in wholeheartedly supporting Abdul El-Sayed for Senate. This election is too important to sow division or stand on the sidelines. We are shocked and heartbroken by Congresswoman Stevens’ decision to support Mike Rogers,” German said .
After a weekend of sparring with el Sayed online over a dispute stemming from their differing opinions on U.S. support for Israel , Stevens endorsed and attended a church service with Rogers.
Michigan Republican Senate candidate Mike Rogers, right, and Rep. Haley Stevens, D-Mich., attend a service at Perfecting Church, Sunday, Nov. 1, 2026, in Detroit. (AP Photo)

Stevens had initially planned on attending a church service with el Sayed in what would have been her first-ever campaign appearance with the Democratic candidate. But after el Sayed’s campaign asked Stevens not to stump with them, Stevens switched gears and backed Rogers.
Stevens, who lost to el Sayed in the race’s Democratic primary, made the stunning reversal after endorsing el Sayed in August.

“As of this morning, many members of our team have resigned, including myself. We encourage everyone to exercise their civic duty, vote for Abdul and Democrats up and down the ballot, and stand up for the America we all believe in,” German said, disavowing Stevens’ cross-party endorsement.

Stevens and el Sayed’s dispute largely centered on an advertisement that Jewish leaders have condemned as antisemitic. The ad, produced by Rebellion PAC, blames the high cost of groceries on U.S. financial support for Israel. Stevens called for el Sayed to denounce the ad and apologize for the anti-Israel allegation.

El Sayed had already distanced himself from the ad, noting that he was not associated with it and accused Stevens of “relitigating” their primary before his campaign asked her to not attend its events. Stevens pointed to this in her endorsement message for Rogers.

“Our Democratic nominee for U.S. Senate, Abdul, said that I was no longer welcome in his campaign and that I should stay away. And he’s right, and that’s why I am endorsing Mike Rogers for the United States Senate today. I don’t belong in Abdul’s campaign. I do not stand with Hasan Piker, who gets trafficked on our college campuses,” Stevens said .
HALEY STEVENS FLIPS ENDORSEMENT TO MIKE ROGERS AFTER SPLIT WITH EL SAYED
Michigan Democratic Party Chairman Curtis Hertel denounced Stevens’s endorsement, stiff-arming her from the party.
“Congresswoman Stevens is not a current member of the Michigan Democratic Party, nor will she be in the future,” Hertel said .

articles.headline: A movie theater plans to hypnotize us into rewatching favorite movies for the first time—but I would just use it for Witcher 3
keyFacts: A Dutch cinema chain called Pathé is hosting an experimental project called REWIND to hypnotize viewers into forgetting their favorite movies.
The project involves thirty moviegoers participating in a session with hypnotherapist Victor Kraemer starting on November 9 at The Hague.
Pathé stated that the procedure is not one hundred percent certain because it remains unclear if hypnosis can actually make someone forget an entire movie.
body: Hypnosis. Fact or fiction? Who knows. Some claim it works wonders, forcing them to quit habits they’ve had for decades or to pick up things they always wanted to do but never could. Others say it’s complete hogwash—a snake oil sale reliant on placebo and your own convictions.
Whether it’s true, I don’t know, but a movie theater seems to believe in its powers to the point of wanting to hypnotize viewers into forgetting their favorite movie.

The reason? You get to watch it for the very first time—again. As reported by Dexerto , a Dutch cinema chain called Pathé is hosting an experimental project called REWIND, which would theoretically allow viewers to mind-wipe and memory-hole their favorite movies and then experience them as if they had never seen them before. The project is taking up 30 moviegoers and kickstarting on Nov. 9 at its Buitenhof venue in The Hague.

It seems to work by bringing people into a session with a hypnotherapist—in this case, Victor Kraemer who apparently has decades of hypnotic experience under his belt—who would then, well, hypnotize you into forgetting. However, Pathé seems to maintain the procedure isn’t 100 percent certain, since it is unclear whether hypnosis can actually make you forget an entire movie. I’m positive it’s even more difficult if you’ve seen the thing dozens of times, as many do with their favorites.

The perfect game. Image via CD Projekt Red If it does work, however, I would love to memory-hole The Witcher 3 from my mind and get to play that masterpiece for the first time again. In 2015, I had a HD 6670 and a dualcore Pentium G2030 supported by six gigs of DDR3 memory, running TW3 at a 12-15 FPS average. It was a horrible experience overall, but even as such, it became my favorite game of all time, to the point where my family invested a lot in a new machine that I bought the year after just so I could play TW3 on high graphics and a great FPS.

The story was just so gripping, so enticing, enthralling even that no amount of poor performance or lag or slow-motion could deter me from playing through it. Between 2015 and 2016 I probably put in over 300 hours in the game on that original hardware , and have come back to replay it time and again over the last 11 years. Blood and Wine is especially close to me, and I can’t even remember (pun intended) how many times I had seen that TW3 trailer with Orianna in it.
It’s the perfect game in almost every way, and I envy those who are yet to try it.

articles.headline: Google is building NASA a robot doctor for use on future deep space missions
keyFacts: Google and NASA are developing a robotic medical assistant to help astronauts handle health emergencies and routine duties on future deep-space missions.
Google executive Jim Kelly said communication delays on deep-space missions complicate emergency medical decisions, making onboard assistance essential.
Google described the project as a proof of concept, requiring further testing before any robot is confirmed space-ready.
body: - Google and NASA are developing a robot to assist astronauts medically
- Deep-space communication delays could make onboard medical assistance essential during emergencies
- NASA's robotic assistant could retrieve ultrasound equipment for astronauts experiencing severe pain
Google is developing a robotic medical assistant with NASA to help astronauts handle health emergencies and routine duties during future deep-space expeditions.
The system is intended to support onboard medical personnel while also performing maintenance, moving equipment, and managing supplies when medical assistance is unnecessary.
The project remains experimental, with laboratory testing indicating progress in basic robotic tasks rather than readiness for autonomous medical procedures.
A robotic assistant for astronauts far from Earth
The project brings together Google Cloud, NASA's Human Research Program, Johnson Space Center's robotics team, and the Jet Propulsion Laboratory to develop robotic assistance for spaceflight.
The work builds on the Crew Medical Officer Digital Assistant, an AI medical support system that Google and NASA have been evaluating since 2025.
That earlier system is designed to help astronauts assess health problems when distance and communication delays make immediate consultation with Earth-based doctors difficult.

“An astronaut on a future deep space mission to Mars could face severe operational challenges, including round-trip communication latencies of up to 44 minutes,” said Jim Kelly, Google's public sector vice president.

Such delays could complicate medical decisions during emergencies, making onboard resources increasingly important when astronauts cannot receive immediate instructions from mission control.
Rather than replacing the crew's medical officer, the robot would assist with practical tasks, leaving diagnosis and treatment decisions under human supervision.
For example, an astronaut experiencing intense back pain possibly associated with kidney stones could request an ultrasound examination using equipment retrieved and prepared by the robot.
The machine could then help position the necessary equipment while the medical officer examines the resulting images and determines the appropriate response.
Early tests show progress, with major limitations remaining
Google is also adapting navigation technology developed at NASA's Jet Propulsion Laboratory to help the robot move through its surroundings and locate equipment.
The team has also used DeepMind's MuJoCo physics simulator to assess movement and object handling before attempting more demanding applications.
According to Kelly, during the initial laboratory trials, the robot achieved an 85% success rate when locating and moving a medical bag.
That result concerns a relatively basic retrieval task and does not establish whether the system can reliably perform medical examinations or assist with complicated emergencies.
“To maximize its utility for a lean crew, the robotic system is designed as a versatile 'payload' handler capable of managing cargo, logistics, and equipment,” Kelly explained.
“When not needed for routine maintenance like organizing tools or securing compartments, it can pivot to medical support.”
Google has described the work as a proof of concept, with early laboratory demonstrations completed but no confirmed fully integrated, space-ready robot.
The agency has declined to provide detailed information about the project, stating that it is examining several advanced AI initiatives with partners for possible future missions.
The robot is also expected to handle cargo, organize tools, secure compartments, and support routine maintenance, allowing a small crew to allocate its time more efficiently.

Google's proposed system therefore combines physical assistance with AI-enabled support, although its practical capabilities will depend on further testing and successful integration with spacecraft operations.
“The ultimate goal is to build a robotic system that can execute a variety of tasks via simple voice instructions, under the astronauts’ direct supervision and command,” Kelly said.
“For instance, the robot might be directed to assist with routine health monitoring—such as capturing basic vitals or simple ultrasounds—under the strict guidance of a human crew medical officer.”

Hawk stated on social media that security shooed them away, making the experience very anticlimactic.

body: Tony Hawk, skateboard legend, video game superstar and the last one to die in the great uprising, has inspired the culture for generations. Since Neversoft put him on the PlayStation in 1999, Hawk has been a household name, the video game series inspiring boarders on the couch and halfpipe alike. Looking to celebrate the 25th anniversary of Tony Hawkâs Pro Skater 3, he traveled to the real world Los Angeles park recreated within the game. Only to be escorted out by security.
“Happy 25th THPS3!” Posted the Birdman himself. “We got kicked out of Pershing Square while shooting this today.”

Though unnamed in the game, the Los Angeles stage of Tony Hawkâs Pro Skater 3 is clearly inspired by Pershing Square, a business park in the cityâs financial district. With its distinctive modernist features from architect Ricardo Legorreta, the stone crescent benches and large red orbs made for a slick backdrop in the 2001 extreme sports game. It still remains in the city today, largely unchanged, as well as the nearby car wash with a big blue obelisk.

As such, recreating the beloved video game should have made for easy content. To the Ramones’ Blitzkrieg Bop, Hawk rolls through Pershing Square, revisiting the sights, recreating the worbling idle stance of his virtual avatar. Leaving most of the tricks to his PlayStation self, Hawk and his team could only film so much before being ejected from the site by security.
“She [security] just shooâd us away,” posted Hawk. “It was very anticlimactic.”

The third entry in the series was the first to hit the PlayStation 2. To this day itâs considered not just one of the best in the series, but is tied with Grand Theft Auto 3 as Metacritic’s best on the console. The game was remade in 2025, part of Iron Galaxyâs Tony Hawk’s Pro Skater 3 + 4 bundle. While the first set was met with a ticker-tape parade, the secondâs reception was a touch milder. Fans young and old continue to be frustrated as getting new, no nonsense entries in any legacy skateboard series feels like pulling teeth, when they could be losing them off a botched rail grind instead.

articles.headline: What remains of canned Portal prequel white whale F-Stop is now fully playable thanks to modders and some big leaks
keyFacts: Assets and source code for the unreleased Portal prequel F-Stop have leaked, making the existing game fully playable.
The Valve Cut Content team and leakers assembled the playable version using the leaked assets, map data, and source code.
Valve originally cancelled the project because it did not test well with audiences, though elements were later used in Portal 2.
body: If you're something of a Portal or Half-Life head, you'll probably already be familiar with F-Stop, an unreleased Portal prequel that remained quite mysterious for many years. Back in 2020, a much deeper look was revealed in a semi-official capacity, revealing a pretty neat concept (that isn't so dissimilar to that of Superliminal). Now, all these years later, assets and source code for the game has leaked, and what exists of F-Stop is fully playable.

As spotted by Kotaku, the Valve Cut Content team and a number of leakers have been able to put together a playable version of F-Stop so that you can try it out for yourself. Mechanically, it works like so: you take a picture of an object, and said object disappears, turning it into a photo. You can then use this photo to rematerialise the object, sometimes changing the scale of it to help you navigate particular puzzles. It's cool! Just not something Valve thought was worth going all in on, evidently.

So the story goes, Valve overlord Gabe Newell did actually quite like the early version of the game that never was, it's just it didn't test all that well. I do kind of think that this is a lesson in not always listening to test audiences; the aforementioned Superliminal really is quite similar in execution, even tonally it's on the same kind of wavelength, and it ended up being quite a tight little experience that ended up being received quite positively, generally. In the end, bits of F-Stop were Frankensteined into Portal 2, so, at least we got that out of it!

The reason for the delay in being able to play F-Stop in this unofficial capacity is because of the crucial source code and map data. Back in August about 12TB of Steam data leaked, but that only contained the assets for F-Stop. Mods in the Valve Cut Content Discord server said that the person who leaked the F-Stop mapsrc asked for $1000 before just handing over the data in any case. Glad they did, $1000 bucks is a lot, I wouldn't pay it myself. Cool little bit of history to be found here, shame it never materialised in the way it was meant to.

articles.headline: Heat Director Michael Mann Hospitalized After Accidentally Shooting Himself in the Leg

body: Heat director Michael Mann was hospitalized with minor injuries after accidentally shooting himself in the leg at a Los Angeles gun range on Halloween.
TMZ confirmed the news with local authorities and the filmmaker's representative today. Mann was reportedly sent to the hospital for treatment and is in the process of being released.

"On Saturday, at a gun range, a weapon accidentally discharged while holstered resulting in a superficial injury to film director Michael Mann," his representative said this morning. "He was treated and is being released."

Mann is known for his role in developing some of the biggest crime dramas of the last 40 years and, as noted by TMZ, is a highly experienced target shooter himself. The site described the incident as having occurred during a training exercise of some kind, with its sources saying the 83-year-old director had no intention of harming himself. Additional details are unclear.

An ambulance ride to the hospital is probably not how Mann wanted to spend his Halloween in Los Angeles. While the accident took a bite out of his weekend, the filmmaker is currently putting the pieces of his long-awaited Heat follow-up together behind the scenes.

Our first big confirmation that the ball was rolling for Heat 2 arrived in February of this year when The Dark Knight star Christian Bale confirmed he was set to start filming the movie in Chicago soon. Inception's Leonardo DiCaprio boarded the project in July, with both he and Bale then reportedly said to play Chris Shiherlis and Vincent Hanna, respectively. Filming was expected to begin in November, this month, at the time.

Mann is also responsible for movies like Ferrari, Public Enemies, and Manhunter. Also expected to appear in Heat 2 are Adolescence's Stephen Graham and The Bear's Ebon Moss-Bachrach. Story details about the follow-up aren't completely clear, though we do know that it will have Mann's novel of the same name to lean on.

While we wait to hear more from Mann, you can check out IGN's 8/10 review of Heat's Blu-ray release. You can also read our 7/10 review of Ferrari. Last month, the director premiered a director's cut of his 2006 film adaptation, Miami Vice. He shed light on his most recent changes during a Q&A at Beyond Fest.

articles.headline: Jagex partnered with a RuneScape-inspired idle game to turn the sequel into an official spinoff
keyFacts: Jagex partnered with developer Games by Malcs to make Melvor Idle 2 an official RuneScape-inspired spinoff.
Jagex stated that the sequel will feature updated visuals and a higher level cap of 120 without any microtransactions.
The upcoming sequel will not take place within the main RuneScape setting of Gielinor.
body: It's easy to knock old-school RPGs, especially grindfests like RuneScape, for being games where you endlessly and sometimes mindlessly make numbers go up. But Melvor Idle, which self-bills as a RuneScape-inspired idle adventure game that claims to squeeze the genre into its "purest form," leans into that—and Jagex has partnered with developer Games by Malcs to make the RuneScape connection official.

The announcement blog from Jagex reads, "Melvor Idle takes a lot of inspiration from RuneScape and you can just feel it," adding that Jagex's support (and branding) is intended to help make the game "even bigger … while Melvor Idle 2 doesn’t take place in Gielinor, we think a fan-built idle game inspired by our MMOs is more than worthy of the title."

This isn't the first time Jagex has collaborated with Games by Malcs. It became the first Melvor Idle's publisher five years ago, albeit without a branding tweak. While RuneScape has had its fair share of monetization controversies over the years (you can see just how skeptical people were of the partnership when it was first announced on Reddit), it doesn't seem like Melvor has been compromised by trouble along those lines—the announcement blog proudly proclaims the sequel will have "no microtransactions."

Beyond that, it seems like a bigger version of the familiar idle RPG with overhauled visuals and a higher level cap of 120. You might find it a bit odd that it's a "RuneScape Adventure" that doesn't take place in the MMO's setting, but I'm not sure how many people are really invested in Jagex's games for the scintillating lore and worldbuilding. If you end up feeling like a stranger in a strange land, you can always hire someone to spam "buying gf" in a chat window while you get your idle on.

articles.headline: At Dead of Night sequel The Great Hugo is coming "(very) soon"
keyFacts: Baggy Cat Games confirmed that the sequel At Dead Of Night 2: The Great Hugo is coming very soon.
The sequel follows Maya five years after the original game as she investigates a Tudor manor house for answers.
The exact release date for the sequel has not yet been announced.
body: Baggy Cat Games, the team behind viral FMV horror game At Dead Of Night, has confirmed that a sequel is "coming (very) soon".
At Dead Of Night 2: The Great Hugo picks up where the original game left off and reunites us with Maya as she heads off to investigate a large Tudor manor house.

At Dead Of Night became famous quickly during the pandemic thanks to streamers and content creators like Markiplier, 8-BitRyan, John Wolfe, and DomPlays, who introduced us to Jimmy Hall, a creepy hotel landlord hellbent on recruiting an audience for his late-night comedy show and psychopathic comedy alter ego, Hugo Punch.
The new game, subtitled The Great Hugo, picks up half a decade later.

"Five years later, Maya is still haunted by her experiences in Sea View Hotel," the blurb teases. "Desperate for answers she remembers the ghost box she used in the hotel, left there when she escaped.

"After searching on [auction] sites and in antique shops, she finds a similar looking device, but can’t get it to work. She contacts an old friend and counsellor, Quinn, who had helped her understand her supernatural experiences in the hotel. Quinn recognises the device and knows where they were made - by an inventor who used to live in a large Tudor manor house not far from Sea View - but warns her against trying to get it working. However, Maya ignores his advice and goes on her own investigation."
Quite how long "(very) soon" is, we don't yet know, but we'll keep you posted.

If you're still in the Halloween mood - and why wouldn't you be; horror games are for life, not just for Halloween - the developer of horror hit The Mortuary Assistant released Playable Archive this week as a Halloween freebie.

As its slightly cheeky title implies, Playable Archive (a riff on the legendary Playable Teaser created for Hideo Kojima's cancelled Silent Hill game) is a small slice of developer Brian Clarke's much larger cancelled Paranormal Activity game, making it a fascinating window into 'what could have been'.

body: Sen. Chris Murphy, D-Conn., was hospitalized after experiencing a stroke, his chief of staff Allison Herwitt said in a statement released Sunday.

Murphy, who is not running in the midterms but has been stumping for Democrats, began feeling numbness in his arm Saturday afternoon while at his son’s hockey game and was taken to a local hospital before being transferred to Johns Hopkins for further monitoring, according to Allison Herwitt.

articles.headline: TechCrunch Mobility: A new, bigger AV boom is here
keyFacts: Trucks VC reported receiving pitches from 81 autonomous vehicle startups in 2026, surpassing previous industry boom years.
Trucks VC said AI foundation models now allow autonomous vehicle startups to deploy within months for under $1 million.
Waymo and Toyota partnered to manufacture autonomous bZ4X vehicles in Japan for robotaxi services in international markets.
body: Welcome back to TechCrunch Mobility, your hub for the future of transportation and now, more than ever, the role AI is playing in it. To get this in your inbox, sign up here for free — just click TechCrunch Mobility!
I’ve joked here and on the Equity and Autonocast podcasts that the autonomous vehicle industry feels a lot like 2016, at least in terms of the buzziness surrounding the sector.

But a recent conversation with Trucks VC partner Puneeth Meruva has me rethinking that comparison. There’s evidence that 2026 is even hotter — at least by certain measures — than those frothy dealmaking days of 2016 and 2017.

Trucks VC, which specializes in early-stage investing, has fielded pitches from 81 new autonomous vehicle startups so far in 2026 — two-thirds more than last year and enough to surpass the boom years of a decade ago. The VC firm argues in a new blog post that we’re in the midst of a second, even bigger AV wave fueled by technological breakthroughs. Yes, I’m talking about AI.

“For a long time AV companies were trying to go from what was AV 1.0 to AV 2.0, which is kind of this holy grail end-to-end architecture for AVs,” Meruva told me. “And I think the foundation models now provide a technical architecture that makes those end-to-end systems possible.”

These foundational models are particularly good at generalizing across different environments and scenarios, potentially making AVs cheaper and faster to deploy. The arrival of powerful open source models like Nvidia’s Alpamayo and Qwen’s general-purpose vision-language-action models has made it even easier for startups to get off the ground.

The barrier to entry is lower than ever before. Meruva said Trucks is consistently seeing startups deploy within a few months and with less than $1 million raised. (And while Meruva wouldn’t name names, the firm has invested in some of them.)

Of these 81 startups that pitched Trucks VC, I mistakenly assumed most would be applying their AV tech to construction, warehouse, agriculture, and mining. And yes, those were in the mix. But what surprised me was the growing number of startups pitching pure-play robotaxi businesses. And many are positioning themselves as direct competitors to Waymo.
As wild and galaxy brain-thinking as that may sound, Meruva thinks there is room for smaller players.

“In this world, smaller, more niche autonomy companies can compete — maybe they’re not competing with Waymo on a global scale, but maybe they’re competing in specific regions or specific types of routes,” he said.
And Meruva doesn’t see the pace flattening. He expects even more AV startups to pitch the firm next year.
Deals!

Regular readers of this newsletter know we’ve been closely following Slate Auto — breaking the original story on Jeff Bezos’ investment way back in April 2025. But the company it spun out of is what got our attention this week.

Re:Build, a Massachusetts-based manufacturing accelerator, raised $2.1 billion to “expand Re:Build’s capacity to manufacture hard tech products and launch new industrial startups.” The investment was led by General Catalyst and JPMorganChase’s Strategic Investment Group. Other investors weren’t disclosed.
The company, which was co-founded by Amazon’s former commercial CEO Jeff Wilke, has billed itself as “America’s answer to Shenzhen.”
Other deals …

Bedrock Robotics raised $600 million in a funding round that values the autonomous vehicle technology startup at $4.1 billion. CapitalG and Emergence Capital co-led the Series C round. New investors US Innovative Technology Fund (USIT), Bessemer Venture Partners, and Temasek participated in the round, alongside existing investors 8VC, Georgian, Valor Equity Partners, Xora, Eclipse, Perry Creek Capital, and Nvidia.
DoorDash has agreed to acquire Instacart for $17 billion. Meanwhile, DoorDash noted in its third-quarter earnings that it has, so far, only received a few hundred orders from AI agents.

PreScalar, a San Francisco-based startup developing software and testing infrastructure for factories, raised $7 million in seed funding co-led by Dynamo Ventures and BMW i Ventures, with participation from Blue Wire Capital, Uplift Ventures, and Antler. The startup was founded last year by a trio who had stints at Cruise, Google, Rivian, and Waymo.
Notable reads and other tidbits
Elroy Air, a startup developing autonomous heavy-cargo drones for defense, rapid response, and commercial logistics, hired Jeremy Hux as its CFO in preparation for going public.
Ford announced two new EV chargers that will allow its forthcoming Fathom pickup truck to serve as a battery capable of delivering power to the home or grid.

GM is embracing hybrids now. Times sure have changed! The U.S. automaker is also trying to move past the driver data-selling controversy from several years ago. GM agreed to a $220 million settlement with 36 states (its settlement with California and the Federal Trade Commission happened earlier) to settle allegations that it illegally sold private driving behavior and location information to data brokers.

Kodiak AI will deliver 75 self-driving trucks to freight company DTL Transport starting in 2028. It’s the company’s first binding commercial deal for driverless big rigs that will run on public highways.

Rivian reported its third-quarter earnings, and a few items stood out to us. For one, the new R2 has been successful enough for the company to raise its 2026 delivery guidance by a couple thousands vehicles. Rivian, which had previously expected to deliver between 65,000 and 70,000 EVs this year, bumped up that floor to 67,000. But here is another potentially lucrative development: The $5.8 billion joint venture between Rivian and Volkswagen Group is expanding to include AI assistants. No word yet on whether that means VW will invest even more money into Rivian.
Tesla turns to Turo to boost adoption of Full Self-Driving (Supervised).

Waymo and Toyota have locked in a manufacturing partnership, officially moving them past the “we’re just talking” phase. Toyota will manufacture AV-ready bZ4X vehicles — and integrate Waymo’s self-driving system — at its factory in Japan. The vehicles will be used for robotaxi services in Japan, the U.K., and other international markets. Importantly, the companies hinted that this could eventually lead to a licensing deal in which Waymo AV tech is in personally owned vehicles.
One more thing …

Last call for founders, investors, and builders based in and around the Boston area. The Founder Summit — a one-day event in Boston — will be held on November 4. And I will be there! This event is really geared toward startup founders, aspiring founders, and investors. Attendees can expect advice-driven talks from VCs and serial founders, plus lots of chances to network.
